concept.title: Resolve Conflicts
concept.shortdesc: When the same lines change on two branches, Git needs your help to decide what to keep.

conbody.p: A conflict happens when a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, or stash apply tries to combine two changes to the same part of a file. Git cannot decide which version to keep, so it pauses and asks you.

The Git Client marks each conflicting file in the
area of the view and keeps the operation in progress until you resolve every one. You have a few ways to do that:

ul.li: Edit the file in the compare editor and choose what to keep, line by line.

Accept one whole side with
or .

conbody.p: Once a file is resolved, the Git Client stages it automatically. When every file is resolved, you can finish the operation. If you would rather back out, you can abort and return to the state before the operation started.
